service_boundary: Represents the Venice developer API and its decentralized or upstream inference routing, not the Venice.ai end-user assistant, upstream model publishers, or customer-operated model deployments.
regional_controls: The reviewed public documentation does not establish customer-selected processing regions; private models run across Venice's decentralized provider fleet, while anonymized models can reach third-party frontier providers.
retention_controls: Venice states that it does not store or log API prompts or model responses. Effective privacy still depends on the selected model tier: private models use Venice-routed GPU capacity, while anonymized frontier models are proxied to third parties under different upstream handling, and selected models offer TEE or client-side E2EE.
routing: Customers select models from a cross-provider catalog. Venice routes private requests across decentralized GPU providers and proxies anonymized requests to frontier providers; response headers can identify the model and router when available.
customization: The service exposes model selection, system-prompt behavior, tools, structured output, and modality-specific generation parameters; arbitrary customer-weight deployment is not established as a public API capability.
strengths: One compatible API spans a large cross-provider and cross-modal model catalog.
Per-model privacy labels plus TEE and E2EE options make inference-boundary differences unusually visible.
tradeoffs: Private and anonymized model modes have materially different upstream boundaries and privacy properties.
The broad, frequently changing catalog requires model-level capability, terms, and retention review.
